provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Allah the Creator
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state that Allah is the Creator.
The pupils should be able to list things Allah creates.

Introduction:
Last term we learned about Allah being one. Today we will learn about Allah as our Creator.

Content:
Allah creates everything. He made the sky, the ground, water, trees and animals. He made you and me. We see Allah's creation when we go to the market and see yams and tomatoes. We see it when we drink water from the well. Allah wants us to care for His creation. We should not waste food or water.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw three things Allah created and name them.

Evaluation questions:
Who creates everything?
Name two things Allah creates.
Why should we care for Allah's creation?

Summary:
Allah is our Creator and we must care for all that He has made.

topics.title: The five pillars
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list the five pillars of Islam.
The pupils should be able to explain Shahadah and salah.

Introduction:
Last week we learned that Allah is our Creator. Today we will learn about the five pillars of Islam.

Content:
The five pillars are the main duties of every Muslim. They are like the five legs of a strong chair. The first pillar is Shahadah. It is saying with your heart that there is no god but Allah and Muhammad is His messenger. The second pillar is salah. It is praying five times every day. We pray facing the Kaaba in Mecca. We pray like the Prophet Muhammad showed us.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice saying the Shahadah together and learn the positions for salah.

Evaluation questions:
How many pillars are in Islam?
What is Shahadah?
How many times do Muslims pray each day?

Summary:
The five pillars help Muslims live a good life according to Allah's rules.

topics.title: Wudu
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why wudu is important.
The pupils should be able to list the steps of wudu.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about salah. Today we will learn how to prepare for prayer by doing wudu.

Content:
Wudu is washing parts of the body before praying. It makes us clean and pure for Allah. Allah loves clean people. The steps of wudu are: wash hands to wrists, rinse mouth, clean nose, wash face, wash arms to elbows, wipe head, wash feet to ankles. We do wudu with clean water like from the well or tap. We must do wudu carefully and think about Allah.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice doing wudu step by step with a partner.

Evaluation questions:
Why do we do wudu?
Name three parts we wash in wudu.
What do we use for wudu?

Summary:
Wudu prepares our body and soul to talk to Allah in prayer.

topics.title: Salah
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the five daily prayers.
The pupils should be able to describe good manners during salah.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about wudu. Today we will learn about salah, the second pillar of Islam.

Content:
Muslims pray five times every day: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib and Isha. We pray at set times. Fajr is before sunrise, Dhuhr is after midday. During salah we stand, bow and prostrate. We face the Kaaba in Mecca. Good manners in prayer are: be on time, dress modestly, focus on Allah, not talk, not look around. When we pray in the mosque with others, we stand in straight rows.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice the positions of salah: standing, bowing, prostrating.

Evaluation questions:
How many times do Muslims pray each day?
Name one time for salah.
What should you do during salah?

Summary:
Salah is talking to Allah five times each day with respect and focus.

topics.title: Surah Al - Fatihah
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al - Fatihah.
The pupils should be able to explain the meaning of Surah Al - Fatihah.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about salah. Today we will learn Surah Al - Fatihah, which we recite in every salah.

Content:
Surah Al - Fatihah is the first chapter of the Quran. It has seven verses. We recite it in every rakat of salah. The meaning is: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. All praise is for Allah, Lord of all worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we worship and You alone we ask for help. Guide us to the straight path. The path of those You have blessed, not of those who deserve anger or go astray.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns reciting Surah Al - Fatihah from memory.

Evaluation questions:
How many verses are in Surah Al - Fatihah?
What do we say in the first verse?
Why do we recite Surah Al - Fatihah in salah?

Summary:
Surah Al - Fatihah is a special chapter that we recite in every prayer to praise Allah and ask for guidance.

topics.title: The Prophet Muhammad
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to describe the life of Prophet Muhammad.
The pupils should be able to state how to follow the Prophet's example.

Introduction:
Last week we learned Surah Al - Fatihah. Today we will learn about Prophet Muhammad, the last messenger of Allah.

Content:
Prophet Muhammad was born in Mecca. He was kind to everyone. He helped poor people. He told people to worship only Allah. He was honest and never told a lie. He was patient when people were unkind to him. He loved children and played with them. He taught us to be good to our neighbors. He showed us how to pray and fast. We should follow his example by being kind, honest and helpful to others.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of Prophet Muhammad doing a good deed.

Evaluation questions:
Where was Prophet Muhammad born?
How did Prophet Muhammad treat children?
Name one way to follow the Prophet's example.

Summary:
Prophet Muhammad was a kind messenger and we should follow his good example in our lives.

topics.title: Honesty in Islam
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why honesty is important in Islam.
The pupils should be able to give examples of honesty.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about Prophet Muhammad. Today we will learn about honesty, which the Prophet always practiced.

Content:
Honesty means always telling the truth. Allah loves honest people. The Prophet Muhammad was always honest. When we are honest, people trust us. Allah is happy with us. Being dishonest is a sin. It breaks trust with Allah and people. Examples of honesty: returning lost money, not stealing in the market, telling the truth even when it is hard. When we are honest, Allah rewards us in this life and the next.

Class activity:
Pupils will role - play situations where they choose to be honest.

Evaluation questions:
Why does Allah love honest people?
Name one example of honesty.
What happens when we are dishonest?

Summary:
Honesty is a good quality that pleases Allah and helps us build trust with others.

topics.title: Kindness to parents
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state the importance of kindness to parents.
The pupils should be able to list ways to serve parents.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about honesty. Today we will learn about being kind to our parents, which Allah commands us to do.

Content:
Allah loves children who are kind to their parents. Our mother and father take care of us when we are small. They feed us, clothe us and teach us. We must respect them and obey them. We should speak to them gently. Ways to serve parents: help with housework, listen to their advice, pray for them, not shout at them, take care of them when they are old. When we are kind to parents, Allah is happy with us.

Class activity:
Pupils will write one kind thing they can do for their parents today.

Evaluation questions:
Why should we be kind to our parents?
Name two ways to serve parents.
What does Allah think about children who are kind to parents?

Summary:
We must always be kind and respectful to our mother and father as Allah commands.

topics.title: Zakat and sharing
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain what Zakat is.
The pupils should be able to describe the importance of sharing.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about kindness to parents. Today we will learn about Zakat and sharing, which are important in Islam.

Content:
Zakat is giving a small part of our money to poor people. It is one of the five pillars of Islam. Allah wants us to share what we have. When we give Zakat, we help people who have no food or clothes. Sharing makes our hearts clean. Allah blesses the wealth we share. We can also share by giving food to neighbors, helping friends with their work, or sharing our toys. When we share, Allah rewards us.

Class activity:
Pupils will draw a picture of sharing something with someone in need.

Evaluation questions:
What is Zakat?
Who do we give Zakat to?
Why should we share what we have?

Summary:
Zakat and sharing are good deeds that help the poor and please Allah.

topics.title: Revision and recitation
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite Surah Al - Fatihah.
The pupils should be able to list the five pillars of Islam.

Introduction:
This week we will revise what we learned this term and practice our recitation.

Content:
We have learned many important things this term. We learned that Allah is our Creator. We learned about the five pillars of Islam: Shahadah, salah, Zakat, sawm and Hajj. We learned how to do wudu and pray salah. We memorized Surah Al - Fatihah. We learned about Prophet Muhammad and his kind life. We learned to be honest, kind to parents and share with others. Let us recite Surah Al - Fatihah together and sing songs of praise to Allah.

Class activity:
Pupils will take turns reciting Surah Al - Fatihah and sing Islamic songs.

Evaluation questions:
What are the five pillars of Islam?
Recite Surah Al - Fatihah.
Name one thing you learned about Prophet Muhammad.

Summary:
We have learned many important lessons in Islamic Studies this term that will help us live good lives.
